settings.description: Continental's flagship winter tire, engineered for Nordic conditions. Quieter than most dedicated winters and holds grip on packed snow at -30°C.
Quiet, long-wearing all-season touring tire. Common OE on European sedans and crossovers — a good choice for high-mileage Deerfoot commuters.

settings.subtitle: Continental is Hannover-engineered for outstanding wet and winter grip — and one of the most balanced premium tire brands on the road. We stock the VikingContact 7 (winter), ExtremeContact DWS06 Plus (performance), and ProContact TX A/S (all-season touring) at 111 42 Ave SW.
settings.intro_heading: Why we recommend Continental in Calgary
settings.intro_richtext:
Continental's been making tires in Germany since 1871. They're the brand most automakers (BMW, Mercedes, Audi, VW) ship as original equipment — which tells you something about consistency and balance.

The VikingContact 7 is Continental's dedicated winter tire — specifically engineered for Nordic winters, which translates well to Calgary's -30°C January nights. Quieter than most dedicated winters, and the rubber compound holds grip on packed snow that Calgary's side streets accumulate before plowing.

For year-round touring on a sedan or crossover, the ProContact TX A/S is a quiet, long-wearing option. For sport sedans that need wet-handling, the ExtremeContact DWS06 Plus has one of the best wet-grip ratings in its class.

Every Continental tire we install gets the same balance, calibrated torque, and TPMS reset as our premium-priced jobs — and we price-match any local Calgary competitor on the same model. Book installation or call (403) 452-4283.

settings.faq_1_q: What's the best Continental tire for Calgary winters?
settings.faq_1_a: The VikingContact 7 is Continental's flagship winter tire — engineered for Nordic conditions, which match Calgary's -30°C cold snaps. We install it from October through April for sedans, crossovers, and SUVs.
settings.faq_2_q: How much do Continental tires cost in Calgary?
settings.faq_2_a: Continental tires at Prince Tires range from $210 to $390 per tire. ExtremeContact DWS06 Plus starts around $215; ProContact TX A/S around $240; VikingContact 7 around $290 in mid-range sizes.
settings.faq_3_a: Yes. The VikingContact 7 carries the 3PMSF symbol, which meets Alberta's winter-tire law and the BC Highway 93 / Trans-Canada Banff winter-tire mandate from October 1 through April 30.
settings.faq_4_q: What's the difference between ExtremeContact DWS06 Plus and DWS06?
settings.faq_4_a: DWS06 Plus is the 2nd-gen model, released in 2019. Better wet-grip and longer treadwear than the original DWS06 (which Continental no longer makes). Both carry the 'DWS' (Dry-Wet-Snow) marking on the sidewall.
settings.faq_5_q: Do you install Continental run-flat tires?
settings.faq_5_a: Yes. We install Continental run-flat (SSR) tires on supported vehicles — BMW, Mercedes, Mini, etc. Run-flats need specific equipment for proper balance and bead seating; we use Hunter Road Force balancers for accurate run-flat install.
settings.faq_6_a: Yes for stocked sizes if you book before midday. Sedan and crossover sizes (215/55R17, 225/45R17, 235/45R18, etc.) are most reliably in stock. Call (403) 452-4283 to confirm before booking trucks or unusual sizes.
settings.calgary_richtext: Continental TrueContact Tour wins the Highway / Touring category for us in Calgary — quiet, low-rolling-resistance, and German-engineered wet grip for the spring slush. ExtremeContact DWS06 Plus is a strong all-season pick for performance sedans. Their winter VikingContact 7 stays soft below -25°C, which is the temperature where rubber compound choice actually matters in southern Alberta.
settings.awards_text: TÜV/Auto Bild summer-tire test winner multiple years. OE supplier to Audi, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen.
settings.testimonial_quote: TrueContact Tour replaced my OE tires on the Audi. Noticeably quieter on Deerfoot, better wet braking in spring slush. Worth the premium.
